subject: RM_Shirrel

reply.subject: RM_Shirrel

observed.facings.png: The owner-kept grounded set (reference only) on one scale. South is a heavy grey-ochre animal facing the camera, with tall tufted lynx ears, a pale chest ruff, slate/cream banded flank folds and a bushy tail swept to the left. East is a low-slung side profile with a long banded flank fold, a hooked muzzle with whiskers, big claws and a long brush tail. North shows the rear: ear backs, banded haunches and the tail hanging down the middle, with no face.
observed.south.png: The grounded front view at full resolution. Face toward the camera, eyes narrowed, lynx ears, a deep pale chest, banded membrane folds on both flanks, heavy clawed forefeet. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: The grounded side profile. Long body with the folded membrane running from the shoulder to the haunch in slate and cream bands, a deep chest, strong curved claws, a whiskered muzzle and a long tail. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The grounded rear. Ear backs, a grey back, cream-banded haunch folds, the tail hanging centrally, hind feet. No eyes or face.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the grounded south sprite stands in a cell beside the vanilla human and is roughly cat-to-small-dog sized: about 0.6 of the cell height, smaller than the human. At 32 px/cell it reads as a small grey creature with ears and a tail, beside the rat.
observed.flight_1.png: East glide frame 1. A side profile stretched flat, legs spread fore and aft, the membrane running wrist to ankle with strong slate/fog-white banding. Head to the right with ears laid back and an open mouth showing teeth, a bushy pale-tipped tail trailing left, curved dark claws on all four feet. Clean alpha.
observed.flight_2.png: East frame 2. Visually the same as frame 1 at this size. Body, head and tail are locked; any billow at the membrane edge is imperceptible.
observed.flight_3.png: East frame 3. Same body and pose. The membrane's lower edge may sag slightly; very subtle.
observed.flight_4.png: East frame 4. Same as frame 2 (ping-pong by design).
observed.flight_5.png: North glide frame 1. Seen from behind and above-behind: two ear backs at the top, the spine running down to a large pale-tipped tail at the bottom, and both membranes spread wide as a flat kite with slate and fog-white bands. Four clawed limbs at the membrane corners. No face.
observed.flight_6.png: North frame 2. Same body. The membrane's leading and trailing edges show a slightly thicker ochre rim, a mild cupping.
observed.flight_7.png: North frame 3. The membrane edges are visibly wavier and scalloped along the leading and trailing rims, with the ochre edge band widened: the billow reads clearly here. Body, tail and head are unchanged.
observed.flight_9.png: South glide frame 1. Face toward the camera with lynx ears and narrowed eyes. Membranes spread to both sides with bold slate/cream banding, clawed hands and feet at the corners, the tail rising behind the head at the top. No face problem. Clean alpha.
observed.flight_10.png: South frame 2. Same body; slight edge billow.
observed.flight_11.png: South frame 3. Same body; the membrane edge cups slightly more.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: flight_9..12 show the face, lynx ears and chest toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: flight_5..8 show the ear backs, the spine and the tail nearest the camera; no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: The north and south glides are seen from slightly above and behind or in front, as a spread kite, which is the natural glide silhouette. The tail and head placement give a clear front/rear read, so neither is a rotated top-down plan.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 19% spread is measured on the owner-kept grounded sprites and comes from pose: the east view is low-slung and the south view upright. Across the flight frames the body occupies a similar span and scale in each direction.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same charcoal/ochre animal with the banded membrane, lynx ears, brush tail and claws in all three directions. The membrane turns with the body: a lengthwise sheet on east, a wide kite on north and south.

SIGNATURE.seen: A full body-length gliding membrane, banded slate and fog-white, is the dominant shape in every frame.

ALIEN.seen: The flight pose recalls a flying squirrel, but the lynx-tufted ears, the storm banding, the oversized claws and the toothy hooked head push it away from a plain Earth squirrel. The grounded set is owner-kept.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Membrane wrist to ankle, banded slate/fog-white: present in all frames. 2) Cat-sized and heavy: the grounded set has the deep chest; the flight body is stretched and reads leaner, especially east, but is still stout through the shoulders. 3) Strong, dark, curved claws on every limb: present.

STYLE.seen: Painterly fur texture with a fine dark outline; not cute (narrowed eyes, bared teeth); not cel, photo or 3D.

OURS.seen: Own artpipe art that matches the kept grounded sprites; not vanilla or donor.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs on a transparent/white ground; no shadow, sky or branch baked in.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The body stays locked across every frame set, with only the membrane edge changing. Frame 4 repeats frame 2. Flight frames sit at the grounded scale. The north frames now show visible cupping and scalloping at the leading and trailing membrane edges, clearest in flight_7, comparable to or stronger than south.

SCALE.seen: Beside the human it is cat-to-small-dog sized, which matches 'cat-sized'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px the spread kite with its pale bands is a bold, distinctive shape; the grounded sprite reads as a small eared creature.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: The grounded reference sprites show the membrane folded along the flanks, symmetric on south and north.

findings.seen: The south membranes carry four or five bold alternating slate/fog-white bands per side; the north membranes show fewer, broader pale bands with more ochre rim. The palette matches but the band count differs.
findings.fix: The north membranes carry the same number and rhythm of slate and fog-white bands as the south membranes.

findings.seen: Stretched flat in the glide, the east body reads fairly slender and squirrel-like; the deep-keeled chest of the grounded east view is hard to see.
findings.quote: cat-sized and heavy-bodied with a deep-keeled chest, not a slim small squirrel
findings.fix: The east glide body shows a deep keeled chest bulging below the membrane line, as heavy as the grounded east sprite.

findings.seen: No body motion is visible. Noted only to confirm that the 1.40 vertical stretch on frame 7 keeps the spine, head and tail locked; it does.

reply.subject: RM_Shirrel
reply.image_seen: Images 1–4 show grounded front, side and rear references of a grey, tuft-eared creature with folded striped membranes; image 5 compares its size with a human; image 6 shows twelve flight frames, grouped east, north and south.

concerns.evidence: North and south both show broad curved fog-white bands separated by slate membrane on each flank. The claimed four or five separate pale membrane bands per south flank are not evident: pale chest fur, limb edges and membrane bands contribute to that impression. The north bands follow the same wrist-to-ankle membrane structure viewed from behind.

In flight_1..4, the east silhouette retains a substantial rounded haunch and a deep chest descending beneath the neck toward the extended forelimb. The horizontal glide stretches its silhouette, but the torso remains substantial. The broad striped flank membrane and projecting claws are also plainly visible.

Across flight_5..8, the ears, central spine, rump and tail retain their positions and shapes. Frame 7 changes the membrane contours, with more pronounced curved leading and trailing edges; frame 8 returns to frame 6's shape. The visible movement belongs to the membranes.
